clue.text: Chevalier's old people

definitions.meaning: Albert Chevalier's music-hall song 'My Old ...' calls his wife his old ...

explanation.surface: A French knight's elderly folk are being described.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Chevalier was a Victorian music-hall singer; his song 'My Old Dutch' uses Cockney slang 'old Dutch' for a wife, so Chevalier's old is 'Dutch'. 'Chevalier' tempts towards France or Maurice Chevalier.
explanation.definitionFit: The inhabitants of the Netherlands are a nation, and Cockney slang 'old Dutch' means a wife, as in Chevalier's song.

clue.text: Dejected journalists fill in document

indicators.note: the reporters fill in the document, sitting inside it

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
the press is journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Downcast reporters complete a form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fill in' looks like completing a form, but it puts PRESS inside DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low and gloomy means being downcast.

clue.text: Mark I want revised

indicators.note: revised says the letters of I want are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A teacher says they want a grade changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a grade; it is Mark Twain, the American author.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain was the pen name of Samuel Clemens, so this is Mark's surname.

clue.text: Liberal workers get order on start of election

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit on top of the following letter

parts.note: hands are manual workers
OM is the Order of Merit

indicators.note: start of takes just the opening letter of election

explanation.surface: A Liberal party's staff receive instructions at the beginning of polling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks political but means generous. OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome gift is a generous one, so the sense is lavish.

clue.text: One has much pleasure following direction supplied by car dealer

indicators.note: the pleasure-giving pair comes after the compass point, following it in the answer

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction
the Roman numeral for one is I
great pleasure is delight

explanation.surface: Someone takes great joy in directions a car salesman gives.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lamp at the front of a car is a standard fitting a dealer would provide.

clue.text: This sort of bowler raises our spirits

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the word for spirits reads it upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: nips are small drinks of spirits

explanation.surface: A kind of bowler hat lifts our mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests a hat; it is a cricket bowler who turns the ball. 'our' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a slow bowler who makes the ball turn off the pitch is this type.

clue.text: Of which this is an expression of meaning

definitions.text: Of which this is an expression of meaning

parts.words: Of which this is an expression of meaning
parts.note: the clue itself is a statement of what a word means, which is what a dictionary entry gives

explanation.definitionFit: A statement explaining a word's sense is precisely what a dictionary entry supplies.

clue.text: Man with cat by weir

definitions.meaning: someone wielding a whip, the cat-o'-nine-tails, flogs people
on the Thames a weir, or the pool below it, is called by this name

explanation.definitionFit: One who flogs with a whip, and an old Thames word for a dam or barrier on the river.

clue.text: US statesman meets a girl

parts.note: a man from the US state of Georgia, a state's man

explanation.surface: An American politician is introduced to a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'statesman' is read as state's man: someone from the US state of Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Leaves carriers by river? That's about right

indicators.note: the river goes about, wrapping around, the letter for right

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Something carries leaves along a river, and that's roughly correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants with trunks bear foliage on their branches.

clue.text: Ugly quarrel took place in court?

definitions.note: cryptic description of a person: the party who took their place in court bringing a case

parts.note: plain can mean unattractive, homely-looking
a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: A nasty row broke out in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic noun phrase, signalled by the question mark: the one who brings the case takes a place in court.
explanation.definitionFit: The litigant who brings a lawsuit appears in court as the complaining party.

clue.text: Reserve in Test or elsewhere

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words Test or elsewhere, spanning two of them

explanation.surface: A substitute player kept in reserve for a Test match or some other game.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock kept back for later use is a reserve.

clue.text: He's about to return home

definitions.note: a man's name, cryptically 'he is' this

indicators.note: the short word for about is to be read backwards, going back the way it came

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A man is on the point of coming back home.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name, so a man could say he is called this.

clue.text: Speaks violently, being given his revision

indicators.note: the letters of given his are put through a revision, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone rants furiously after being handed a corrected version of their work.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail against something is to protest with bitter, vehement words.

clue.text: Coroner's sort of death note, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a coroner may give a verdict of death by misadventure, not intended
in music a sharp, flat or natural sign outside the key signature

explanation.definitionFit: A coroner may record a death as unintended; in music a sign changing a note's pitch outside the key is also called this.

clue.text: Extract wanted from Moby Dick?

parts.note: not a passage from the novel but the waxy substance whalers sought from a sperm whale like Moby Dick

explanation.definitionFit: Whalers hunted the sperm whale for the waxy oil in its head, a prized product.

clue.text: Furniture Casey adapted with locks

indicators.note: adapted means the letters of Casey are altered into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: locks are tresses of hair

explanation.surface: A man named Casey modified some furniture to include locks.
explanation.definitionFit: A comfortable armchair is an item of furniture.

clue.text: Part for a player

definitions.meaning: a portion, one of two equal shares
a ...-back or fly-... in football or rugby is called a ...

explanation.definitionFit: One of two equal portions; also the name of a footballer or rugby player in the midfield positions.

clue.text: Sort of writer not bound to make cuts

parts.note: free means not tied or bound
to lance is to cut open, as with a boil

explanation.surface: A kind of author, under no contract, is allowed to edit.
explanation.definitionFit: An author working for various clients without a permanent contract is self-employed.

clue.text: Nets luce — could be eatable

indicators.note: could be says the letters of Nets luce might become another word when reordered

explanation.surface: Netted pike might be fit to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: A luce is a pike, a freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word for edible, fit to be eaten as food.

clue.text: "Fear in a handful of -" (Eliot)

parts.note: a famous line from T S Eliot's The Waste Land; the missing word completes the quotation

explanation.walkthrough: The line is 'I will show you fear in a handful of ...' from The Waste Land.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliot's line ends with the word for fine powdery dirt, evoking mortality.

clue.text: Lower climb, but might be grand practice

parts.note: minor means lesser or lower in rank
to scale is to climb

explanation.surface: A lesser ascent, yet it could be excellent training for climbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' is a grand piano, not 'excellent': pianists practise scales.
explanation.definitionFit: Pianists rehearse scales as exercises, and one in a sad-sounding key could be played on a grand piano.

clue.text: Castor or Pollux for example upset by pain

parts.note: Castor and Pollux were the twin sons of Leda in Greek myth

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the abbreviation upside down, reading it upwards

explanation.surface: One of the mythical twins is troubled by an ache.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden sharp pang is a brief stab of pain.

clue.text: Dickensian mineral brew, possibly

parts.note: mica is a mineral that splits into thin sheets

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of brew could be rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: A drink made from minerals, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilkins Micawber is the optimistic debtor in David Copperfield, a character created by Dickens.

clue.text: One may be struck in contest

definitions.meaning: a small stick lit by striking it
a game or competition between two sides

explanation.definitionFit: A stick lit by striking, and a game between rivals, share the same name.

clue.text: Sea-food to give us strength, : say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word for strength is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: muscle means physical strength

explanation.surface: Seafood is offered to make us strong.
explanation.definitionFit: A bivalve shellfish eaten as seafood, often steamed in wine.

clue.text: Workers distributed fish to East End

indicators.note: distributed spreads the letters of fish into a new order
End takes the last letter of East

explanation.surface: Labourers handed out fish to the poorer part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East End' looks like the London district, but End picks the last letter of East. 'distributed' rearranges FISH into SHIF.
explanation.definitionFit: A group working a set period in a factory is a team of workers on the same rota.

clue.text: Wed heartless girl

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the word for wed is taken out

parts.note: to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: A cruel young woman gets married.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Drill connected with explosives?

definitions.meaning: to drill is to ... or coach by repeated exercise
a line of gunpowder laid to carry fire to a charge

explanation.definitionFit: To drill soldiers is to coach them; a fuse line of gunpowder leading to a charge is also called a train.

clue.text: Actor of old appeared in 26 parts

indicators.note: parts suggests the letters are broken into pieces and reassembled in another order

parts.note: aged means old
the answer to 26 across, a word for drill

explanation.surface: An old-time actor took roles in twenty-six productions.
explanation.walkthrough: '26' stands for that clue's answer, TRAIN; 'parts' mixes AGED and TRAIN together. 'of' and 'appeared in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer specialising in serious drama is an actor of that kind.

clue.text: Ragging might give some outsider entertainment

parts.note: in racing an outsider is a horse not expected to win
a play is a dramatic entertainment

explanation.surface: Teasing could provide amusement for someone left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough boisterous fun, like teasing and tormenting, is rowdy play.

clue.text: Sir Tom Jones also?

definitions.meaning: an honorific prefix given to a knight
Tom Jones is the name of Fielding's novel, so a book's name

explanation.definitionFit: Sir is a form of address given to knights, and Tom Jones is the name of Fielding's novel.
